label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/snapbug.mdl, models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, C, B, D where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Outline matches the brief's drum: an upright cylinder about 1.55 times as tall as it is wide, flat top and bottom, with the rim bands visible in every side view. Nothing sticks out or is missing in any of the ten views.

M2.reason: Measured 22.6 x 22.6 x 35 against the brief's 23 across and 34 high: 1.7% off across and 2.9% off high, well inside 15%.

M3.reason: The brief's parts are present: the drum body, the rust bands at the top and bottom rims, and the hazard stripe. The top view shows a flat lid with no bung openings, and a real 55-gallon drum has two. The rims are a bevel with no raised chime beads. Those small parts are missing, which caps M3 at 1. The top and bottom disks read as roughly 14 sides, and the brief gives no side count to check that against.

M4.reason: The rust is correct in its places, on the top and bottom rim bands, and the stripe is yellow and black. But the body is a clean, even blue-grey paint with only faint mottling, so the drum reads as a blue painted drum with rusty rims rather than the 'rusted' drum the brief asks for. The rust needs to cover more of the body.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe is sharp and well placed, and the rust is speckled. A vertical texture seam runs through the stripe at the centre of the front view and at the front-left and front-right views, where the stripe does not line up. The body paint is soft and smeared, so the detail is weaker than the stripe and rust suggest.

M6.reason: Capped by the line-up test, which the asset passed: judges picked C, C, B and D where the asset was D, A, C and C, so it was never caught as the one not made by Valve. In the line-up it reads as a game prop beside the three of Half-Life's own.

M7.reason: A drum has no front. It stands upright on its bottom disk, and its origin sits at the base, as a drum's does. Its rotation about the vertical axis matches the brief.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. Triangles: 96, under the 198 allowed (twice Half-Life's median of 99, which is more than the 156 three-quarters line). Both the top and bottom disks are closed in every view, and nothing floats or looks inside out.
